title: 'Thank you, Dixie': Baytown Police K9 'Dixie' dies after cancer battle
text:
The Baytown Police Department said goodbye to a K9 officer that had served with the department since 2019.
Man buys $25,000 Camaro, learns months later it was stolen and allegedly sold through HPD auction Body found during search for missing 74-year-old man who disappeared looking for crashed remote-controlled plane – The Baytown Police Department said goodbye to a K9 officer that had served with the department since 2019.
“Donated to us by the Jimmy Ryce Foundation and coming from Bluegrass Bloodhounds in Leitchfield, Kentucky, Dixie quickly became an important part of our K9 Unit and our community,” the department said. Along with her handler, Corporal Shedd, Dixie became certified through the National Police Bloodhound Association in October 2020. Together, they responded to searches for missing children, seniors living with Alzheimer’s or dementia, and suspects attempting to avoid arrest.
“For nearly seven years, Dixie served alongside Corporal Shedd, building a bond that went far beyond the badge. She was a partner, a protector and a beloved member of the department,” the department said. After a battle with cancer, the department said Corporal Shedd made the difficult decision to let Dixie rest peacefully.
“While saying goodbye is never easy, we are grateful for the years of service, dedication and companionship she gave to Corporal Shedd, our K9 Unit and our Baytown community. We know this loss is especially difficult for Corporal Shedd, who cared for and worked alongside Dixie throughout her career," the agency said.
“We ask our community to keep Corporal Shedd, her family, and the entire K9 Unit in your thoughts as they grieve the loss of their partner and friend. ”Christian Terry covered digital news in Tyler and Wichita Falls before returning to the Houston area where he grew up. He is passionate about weather and the outdoors and often spends his days off on the water fishing.
